chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever issues a fatwa to the people without knowledge and without guidance — the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment curse him, and the burden of those who acted upon his fatwa is attached to him.

key_terms.أَفْتَى: To issue a fatwa — a formal religious legal opinion. In the early Islamic context, this was a highly responsible act requiring mastery of scripture, tradition, and jurisprudential reasoning.
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ وَ مَلَائِكَةُ ا: The angels of mercy and angels of punishment — representing the two extremes of the angelic realm. Being cursed by both means there is no refuge or mitigation.
key_terms.هُدًى: Guidance — in the Shia tradition, this refers to divinely-granted guidance, particularly from the Imams (AS). Issuing rulings without such guidance means acting outside the sanctioned religious authority.
key_terms.وِزْر: Burden/sin — the moral and eschatological weight of a wrongful act that is transferred to the one responsible. The concept implies ongoing accountability for consequences one has set in motion.

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about issuing fatwas without knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delivers a stern warning against issuing religious rulings without proper knowledge or divine guidance. The severity of this sin is underscored by the dual curse — from both the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment — making it a transgression that finds no intercessors. Furthermore, the one who issues such a fatwa bears the accumulated sins of every person who followed it, multiplying his accountability.
word_analysis: issues a fatwa/gives a religious ruling

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Ubeda Al Haza’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who issues Fatwa to the people without knowledge and without (having) guidance, the Angels of the Mercy and the Angels of the Punishment curse him, and attach him with the burden of the ones who acted by his Fatwa’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Ri’ab from abu ‘Ubayda al-Hadhdha’ from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following. “

The angels of mercy and the angels of wickedness condemn those who give to people fatwas without knowledge and guidance. Such people will be held responsible for the sins of all those who have followed such fatwas.”
